Influence of model terms on the composition

Source: R/influence.R
influ_comps.Rd

For each term, computes (1) the effect of each level on every bin, (2) the distribution of the data over the levels by year, and (3) the influence of the term on the annual composition. The influence is the log ratio of the annual proportion in each bin predicted with the term at the observed levels to the proportion predicted with the term at its reference. The same quantity is also given for a statistic of the composition (by default the mean bin). The design follows the coefficient-distribution-influence plots used for CPUE standardisation.

Usage

influ_comps(
  fit,
  scale_df = NULL,
  predvar = "catch",
  grps,
  by,
  terms = NULL,
  grid = NULL,
  selectivity = NULL,
  reference = NULL,
  weight = NULL,
  density = NULL,
  stat = "mean",
  components = c("catch", "index")
)

Arguments

fit

A ComPoM object from fit_model() with backend = "TMB".

scale_df, predvar

Data frame and weight column for the catch component; see scale_comps().

grps

Grouping variables for the scaling; see scale_comps().

by

Variable in grps (or grid) over which the statistic is plotted, usually the year.

terms

Terms to evaluate. Default: the ffx_form and re_form variables except by.

grid, selectivity, reference, weight, density

Settings of the index component; see scale_comps().

stat

"mean" (default), a probability between 0 and 1 for a quantile of the bin (e.g. 0.9), or a function of bin and p. See comp_quantile().

components

Components to compute: "catch" and/or "index".

Value

A list of class comp_influ with data frames effects (log multiplier by term, level and bin), distribution (share of the weight by term, level, component and year), influence (log ratio by term, component, year and bin) and influence_stat (difference in the statistic by term, component and year).

Details

The influence is computed for the catch component (mode = "catch" in scale_comps()) and the index component (mode = "index"). Terms in selectivity have no influence on the index by construction and are given zero influence for that component. Random effects are removed with the TMB backend only together, so that with more than one random-effect variable they form one term (labelled with all variables). Effects of covariate smooths and spatial fields are not included; see cvar_smooth_plot() and spatial_field_plot().

See also

plot_cdi_comps(), step_comps()

Examples

# \donttest{
dat <- data_prep(ex_comp, c("Year", "Season", "Vessel", "trip"), "length", "count")
fit <- fit_model("Year + Season", "Vessel", data = dat, backend = "TMB",
                 iter = 300, warmup = 100, thin = 2)
#> Model formula: tot_by_bin ~ 0 + bin + factor(Year):bin + factor(Season):bin + (1 | bin:Vessel)
inf <- influ_comps(fit, scale_df = ex_catch, predvar = "catch",
                   grps = c("Year", "Season", "Vessel"), by = "Year",
                   terms = "Season")
plot_cdi_comps(inf, "Season")

# }
